+1

1. Cloudflare Registrar — my pick

If you're reasonably comfortable with technology, I'd buy the domain here.

The biggest advantage is that Cloudflare isn't trying to make money by heavily marking up your domain renewal. It sells domains at cost. 
Cloudflare

It's also excellent if your website will eventually use:

Vercel

AWS

Google Cloud

Shopify

custom DNS

CDN/security

email services like Google Workspace

Downside: the interface is more infrastructure-oriented. If you've never touched DNS before, Namecheap/GoDaddy feels more beginner-friendly.

2. Namecheap — best balance

I'd choose Namecheap if you want something simple but don't want the GoDaddy ecosystem.

It's particularly nice for someone buying:

1–5 domains

.com, .ai, .in, etc.

domains for future projects

domains with privacy protection

Namecheap includes domain privacy for free on eligible domains. 
Namecheap

The downside is that its renewal pricing is higher than Cloudflare's at-cost model. For example, Namecheap currently lists .com renewal at $18.48. 
Namecheap

3. GoDaddy — easiest for a non-technical business owner

GoDaddy is probably the easiest if you want:

Domain → Website → Business email → Hosting → Everything in one account

It's very established in India and has an India-specific storefront/support ecosystem. 
GoDaddy

But I wouldn't choose it just for domain registration.

The classic GoDaddy issue is:

Cheap first year → considerably more expensive renewal → lots of add-ons.

GoDaddy itself notes that low introductory domain pricing doesn't necessarily mean the renewal rate will be the same. 
GoDaddy

What I'd choose for you

If you're buying a domain for a startup/business brand rather than just a hobby website:

🥇 Cloudflare

Best long-term choice

🥈 Namecheap

Best if you want the easiest domain-only experience

🥉 GoDaddy

Best if you want an all-in-one small-business package

And importantly, you don't need to buy your hosting from the same company as your domain registrar.

For example:

Cloudflare
→ yourcompany.com

Vercel
→ hosts website

Google Workspace
→ hello@yourcompany.com

That's actually the setup I'd recommend for a modern startup.
